audit_logging_summary: Customer requirements (detailed): SIEM export: support Splunk HEC (JSON over HTTPS) + RFC5424 syslog. Export must support batching and checkpointing. Log schema: flat JSON with canonical fields: '@timestamp', 'tenant_id', 'request_id', 'correlation_id', 'api_key_hash', 'model', 'model_version', 'endpoint', 'latency_ms', 'tokens_in', 'tokens_out', 'prompt_hash', 'response_hash', 'status', 'error_code', 'redaction_flags', 'storage_ref'. Access logs: include source_ip, vpc_endpoint_id, subnet_id, egress_region, tls_cipher, client_cert_subject, idp_subject_id. Retention: configurable lifecycle — hot searchable tier (30/90/365 days) then cold archive with immutability for 7 years. Export destinations: Splunk, Elastic, SumoLogic, remote syslog collectors; must support HEC token rotation. KMS: BYOK required, envelope encryption for archived blobs, key rotation policy documented; HSM-backed key option mandatory for PHI. Audit integrity: support signed log digests or append-only ledger (digest chain) for tamper evidence. Access controls: role-based export permissions, signed export tokens, and support for IP allowlists and mTLS on ingest endpoints. Compliance notes: ISO27001 + SOC2 controls must be demonstrated; provide sample audit report and retention attestation for legal. PII redaction: two-tier approach — inline redaction for exported logs + encrypted forensic bucket for full content accessible only via audited workflows.
